_comment: THE ANDROID DEVICE THIS FRAMEWORK IS VERIFIED AGAINST - one definition, read by
both the local tooling and the runtime check, so 'it passed locally' means
something.
⚠️ WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. On a real project the local AVD and the CI agent agreed
on everything a test can see EXCEPT the screen:
local                        CI
API level    35                           35
image tag    google_apis                  google_apis
profile      pixel_7                      pixel_7
ABI          arm64-v8a                    x86_64   (must match the host)
The screen is the one to close, because a CI framebuffer override usually exists
for the agent's sake (fewer pixels for a GPU-less host) and nothing applies it
locally. Note the direction: CI had MORE logical room, so the difference made CI
more forgiving about what is above the fold, not less.
⚠️ SCREEN SHAPE IS LOAD-BEARING ON ANDROID, and this is the reason to pin it.
Android's page source holds only what is LAID OUT. A section that is off-screen
is not in the tree at all - so a test that scrolls to a title and then reads its
lower children passes on one screen size and fails on another. iOS does not
behave this way, which is how such a bug reaches CI green locally.
⚠️ ABI IS DELIBERATELY NOT PINNED, and it is the one thing that cannot match.
The emulator must run the HOST's architecture or it translates every guest
instruction - arm64-v8a on Apple Silicon, x86_64 on Intel CI agents. Both sides
derive it from `uname -m`.
scripts/android-emulator.mjs creates and boots exactly this; wdio.conf.ts
fingerprints the attached device and warns when it differs.
⚠️ IF YOUR CI RESTATES THESE VALUES - because its config language cannot read a
JSON file - keep the two in step. The fingerprint is what catches you if you
don't. See docs/guides/ci.md.
